A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, renamed from AmodalGen3D to GENA3D. Their complete main texts, equations, tables, figures, and appendices are readable and support comparison despite extensive reformatting.

before.justification: v1 reports original GSO reconstruction results, component and input-view ablations, and qualitative evaluations on synthetic and real-world scenes, including appendix examples.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experiments and adds SAM3D comparisons, coherence and visible-region fidelity measurements, and an appendix occlusion-severity experiment.

M1.justification: The two-stage architecture, visibility-weighted view fusion, geometry-gated stereo attention, pretrained SLAT stage, and flow-matching objective remain unchanged. v2 omits v1's optional monocular-depth alternative in Section 3.2, but does not specify a replacement or establish that the implemented single-view procedure changed.

E1.justification: Training on 3D-FUTURE and ABO and evaluation on GSO, Hypersim, COCO, and Mip-NeRF 360 remain. Appendix B.1 adds controlled occlusion-severity conditions on GSO, modestly extending the tested input conditions within the existing task. The highest severity is inconsistently described as 75% in prose and 70% in the table.

E2.justification: v2 adds SAM3D to the existing comparator set: single-view quantitative results appear in Tables 1 and 2, and qualitative comparisons appear in Figure 5 and Appendix Figure B.1. Figure 5 includes multi-view examples, with an MV-SAM3D adaptation mentioned in Section 4.2. Existing baselines remain.

E3.justification: Evaluation expands substantially through visibility-masked SSIM, PSNR, and LPIPS, plus a Qwen3-VL-based Perceptual Coherence Score using eight rendered views. Appendix B.1 introduces a 500-object subset evaluated at controlled occlusion levels with one and two input views. Existing training and main GSO settings remain. The 70% versus 75% discrepancy leaves the highest new test severity unresolved.

E4.justification: Appendix B.1 adds an occlusion-severity sensitivity study, and Appendix B.4 adds SAM3D failure examples concerning observation fidelity and plausible completion. The original component, view-count, completion-backend, and MVS-error analyses are retained, including their numerical results.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, experimental seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests. Averaging the new coherence scores across objects does not introduce uncertainty reporting.

E6.justification: Original benchmark and ablation values remain, but v2 adds substantial results for SAM3D, PCS, visible-region fidelity, and occlusion severity. The method's original FIDs remain 33.91, 32.12, and 30.73; new PCS values are 61.9, 66.3, and 67.0. Added comparisons also reveal exceptions to superiority: single-view SAM3D has lower MMD than ours, 5.50 versus 5.68, and lower LPIPS, 0.226 versus 0.231.

T1.justification: Equations 1–7 retain the same attention, fusion, geometry-conditioning, and flow-matching definitions. No formal assumptions, theorems, proofs, or derivations are added. The new PCS rubric is an empirical evaluation procedure rather than a mathematical development.

C1.justification: Despite the generation-focused title and rewritten framing, both versions claim complete, coherent amodal 3D objects from sparse unposed observations through the same two conditioning mechanisms, with superior empirical quality. The central task, contributions, and claimed capabilities remain substantively unchanged.

C2.justification: v2 newly explains view fusion through the base generator's canonical-pose property and contrasts active attention regulation with passive geometry conditioning. It also interprets the new occlusion tests as robustness evidence and SAM3D examples as supporting the proposed combination of priors. Both conclusions retain the limitation that plausible hidden geometry need not match ground truth.

D1.justification: Appendix A.3 adds the Qwen3-VL 32B evaluator, rendering procedure, scoring rubric, aggregation rule, and complete PCS prompt. Core architecture, preprocessing, hardware, and training details remain unchanged. The optional monocular-depth guidance note is removed, and the printed project address changes with the rename; changed resource availability is not established.

R1.justification: v2 adds references for SAM3D, Qwen3-VL, SSIM, LPIPS, and COCO4D, while removing MoGe and three unposed-MVS references. It sharpens the positioning of MVS as a structural prior for generation. The broader related-work coverage and relationship to Amodal3R and TRELLIS remain.

P1.justification: The paper is renamed, and the abstract, introduction, mechanism explanations, and conclusion are extensively rewritten around generative plausibility and geometric coherence. Reconstruction terminology is systematically revised, related-work subsections are reordered, and the appendix gains new subsections.

P2.justification: The document changes from two-column to single-column layout, extensively resizing and relocating figures and tables. Table 1 gains SAM3D and PCS, new Tables 2 and B.1 and Figure B.1 are added, and Figure 5 gains SAM3D comparisons and revised examples. Original appendix image grids are retained as Figures B.2–B.5.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens evaluation of the retained method through a relevant new comparator, direct visible-region fidelity measurements, and controlled occlusion testing. The documented PCS procedure also makes that addition inspectable. These gains are tempered by the unresolved 70%/75% test severity, underspecified multi-view SAM3D adaptation, and lack of validation for the VLM score. Overall, the evidence becomes more informative, with a limited net quality improvement.
